name_note: The literature genus Blautia is broader than GTDB R232 g__Blautia, which excludes species such as Blautia wexlerae and Blautia luti (placed in the separate GTDB genus Blautia_A), so genus-level statements below describe the genus as the cited sources define it.

sentences.text: Blautia is described as a genus of anaerobic bacteria that occur widely in the feces and intestines of mammals.
A taxonomic study proposed Blautia as a new genus and transferred several species, including Ruminococcus hansenii and Ruminococcus productus, into it.

Blautia stercoris was described from a strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive bacterium isolated from the faeces of a healthy individual, whose glucose fermentation produced acetic acid as the major short-chain fatty acid.
A cross-sectional study of Japanese men and women aged 20-76 years reported Blautia as the only gut microbe inversely associated with visceral fat area in both sexes.
